title: File card: name and size, readable by the bot
gate: Gate A oracle-file-sent 77/78 (the file card: card#3, 10 parts; scripts/lib/cards.mjs), oracle-file-waiting 66/66 (the file waiting in the composer); behaviour 7 file rules (scripts/behaviour.mjs) and 5 open-file rules (scripts/lib/open-files.mjs); live npm run turn:live -- --file and -- --file --pdf (parity/live/file.json)
evidence: The sent card looks as the oracle's 1.0.3 card (fixtures/states/oracle-file-sent, a version exception, docs/decisions/0008): components/Cards.tsx FileCard + styles/cards.css, in a row of its own above the message's bubble: 300 x 72 on rgb 37, radius 22, a page mark (a sheet with four lines), the name (its kind kept apart so a long name loses its middle) and the size. Waiting, a file sits inside the composer above the words as the oracle's does (components/Attachments.tsx: half the row, 56 tall, page mark, name, size, a Remove button; the box grows to 136, radius 18). The composer takes pictures, text files and PDFs, four in all, 3 MB each, by Attach files, a paste or a drop (Composer.tsx); each is stored for the conversation at the send (chat/api.ts uploadAttachment; Barkpark reads the type from the bytes), and the message names a picture by id and a file by {id, name} (sendMessage). A file Barkpark refuses (400), or a computer that cannot take files (422 host_cannot_receive_attachments), sends nothing: a plain line says why and the words and the file stay in the box. The sent message shows the file card at once, and after a reload from the stored row (Barkpark's attachments[] carries the name; chat/useConversation.ts). scripts/behaviour.mjs: 3 picture rules, 7 file rules (a zip refused, nothing stored; a file's kind fitted on its exact text only, ".md" at the name's 0.14px and ".txt" at its own -0.2px (Cards.tsx KIND_FIT, measured on oracle-file-waiting's 20.9); a text file waits by name and size; Enter stores it once and names it by id and name, the card shows; a 400 keeps the draft; a 422 keeps the draft and the same draft then goes (control); a reload shows the card from the row, once). Live pictures: npm run turn:live -- --picture (2026-11-13; parity/live/picture.json). Live files (parity/live/file.json): a text file and a one-page PDF made in the script, each holding only a code made up for the run; the bot replied with the code, and the message showed the file card by name and size, also after a reload (text 2026-11-15, 23 bytes, 7.5 s; PDF 2026-11-14, 596 bytes, 9.3 s). Still missing (not in the title): the size wording past bytes: a byte size reads "25B" as the oracle's card does (seen by the lead on the oracle-file-sent screenshot, 2026-11-14; chat/useConversation.ts fileSize; behaviour pins "24B"), but "KB" and "MB" are ours, written the same way, not read from the oracle. Opening a file from its card works (task-71ee600273461306): a press or Enter opens it in a new tab at /api/chat/<session>/attachments/<id>, whose headers decide the rest, as Barkpark's TicketsAttachmentsController does: a text file (text/plain; charset=utf-8) and a PDF (application/pdf) both download, never drawn here (Chrome's PDF viewer runs a PDF's own script under the page's origin and ignores a CSP sandbox, rev299 on #317; a file can land on a bot's reply too), with nosniff and a CSP sandbox as Barkpark's ticket route sends; Barkpark stores HTML, SVG and script as text/plain, and any other type is a 415 (scripts/lib/open-files.mjs: 5 rules). What the oracle's own card opens is not captured, so the browser's tab stands in. On 1.2.3 (decision 0010) oracle-file-sent is 77/78 and oracle-file-waiting 66/66. The miss left in file-sent is the time row: "Today 11:31 PM" 4.1 wider in the stand-in face (F6; no spacing is fitted to it, T2). Within the 1 pt tolerance, file-waiting still differs: the answered card's question text is 0.1 wider and 0.5 shorter, "Cedar" 0.4 narrower (the stand-in font), and every row sits 0.5 higher, because Grok's list was scrolled 0.5 short of its end in that capture (content ends 760.5 in a 760 window). The reply under a card starts its bubble 10 into its row, as file-waiting, file-sent, pictures-sent and voice-picker-start all show (styles/cards.css; it was 11, fitted to choice-answered alone).
